ORAL JUDGMENT Aggrieved by the award passed in M.V.C.No.192/2019 dated 03.12.2021 by the Senior Civil Judge and AMACT, Holalkere, whereby the Court had granted compensation of an amount of Rs.4,16,005/- the claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of the compensation by filing M.F.A.No.5787/2022 and the KSRTC is before this Court by filing M.F.A.No.2790/2022 questioning the entire liability fixed on the KSRTC when there is a negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry.

2. Learned counsel appearing for the KSRTC submits that the accident had taken place in the midnight when the lorry was parked on the road without the parking lights on and because of his negligence, the accident had occurred and with considering this particular aspect, the Tribunal had fastened the liability on the driver of the KSRTC.
It is submitted that the KSRTC has also examined the Depot Manager and driver in support of the case and all these aspects are not considered by the Court.
NC: 2025:KHC:34535 HC-KAR 3.

Learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that though the claimant had sustained two fracture injuries, the Court under the head of pain and suffering had not granted reasonable compensation.

Further, when he had sustained 18% disability, the Court had granted very meagre amount under the head of loss of amenities and on all other heads also, the amount that is awarded by the Tribunal is not just and reasonable.
4. Having heard the learned counsels on either side, perused the material on record.

5. Coming to the negligence and liability, the Tribunal had observed that on perusal of evidence of PW.1, RW.1 and RW.2 and Exs.R1 and R2, it is forthcoming that the manner in which the accident had taken place and involvement of both vehicles especially in Ex.R2 rough sketch, the place of occurrence is shown that the accident had occurred due to the involvement of KSRTC bus itself.

At the same time, the place in which insured lorry is shown at a remote point towards western site at Rudranna vs The Managing Director/Divisional ... on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154924558/
4 the distance of 100 metres from the spot.
The Investigating Officer had rightly submitted the charge sheet NC: 2025:KHC:34535 HC-KAR against the driver of the KSRTC bus.
Respondent Nos.3 and 4 are subsequently brought on record and it will not take away the evidence as per Ex.R2, which points out against the driver of the KSRTC bus.
Hence, the Tribunal had come to the conclusion that the accident had taken place because of the negligence of the driver of the KSRTC bus and the KSRTC is alone liable to pay the compensation.

6. In the light of the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the KSRTC, this Court has perused the sketch and the charge sheet, which clearly points out at the negligence of the driver of the KSRTC bus and this Court do not find any reasons to interfere with the said finding of the Tribunal.
7. Then coming to the claimants appeal, he had sustained two injuries.
Under the head of 'pain and suffering', this Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.60,000/-.
Towards medical expenses no interference is called for.

As the claimant was admitted in the hospital for 8 days and considering 8 days of hospitalization, this Court is granting an amount of Rs.8000/- under the head of 'attendant charges'.
NC: 2025:KHC:34535 HC-KAR

Coming to the loss of income during the laid up period, as the accident had taken place in the year 2018, this Court is taking the income at Rs.12,500/-, 'loss of income during the laid up period' would come to an amount of Rs.37,500/- (Rs.12,500/- x 3).
Towards loss of future income, the Court had rightly considered the evidence of the doctor and rightly granted the compensation and no interference is called for.

Considering 18% of disability,
this Court is granting Rs.25,000/- under the head of 'loss of amenities'.
8.

In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V.Mekala Vs. M.
Malathi And Another1, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards 'Legal Expenses'.
9.
